bull_bear.body:
- Funding: internal accruals + bank debt/facilities; equity raise not ruled out but not the current plan ("whatever makes commercial sense for Board/shareholders").
- Emphasis on capital discipline, avoiding unnecessary gearing dilution; capex historically self-funded by cash generation.
- 40% Adbhoot producing-property stake acquired; increased B-80 participating interest.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Pipeline dependency** (biggest): Dirok evacuation depends on Assam Gas Co / NRL / Oil India third-party DNPL line; 55 km bad patch laid but not yet tied in (needs NRL shutdown); Oil India publicly signalled DNPL may stay non-common-carrier — HOEC's gas access uncertain. Full DFL–Duliajan line 2–3 yrs out.
- **HPCL crude dispute**: invoice reversed, crude resold to third parties at Brent-minus-X, proceeds over 2–3 months; conciliation per COSA pending; potential loss vs March inventory valuation (mgmt says downside factored).
- **Funding** not yet secured for capex ramp.
- **Rig/diesel availability & weather** could slip drilling 3–6 months.
- New, unproven management team; aggressive 1.5 → 32 kboe/d ramp.
- Loss-making FY26.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - First call for new MD Baroruchi Mishra; brought in heavyweight ex-Shell/BG/PTTEP team (CFO Andrade 40 yrs, offshore head Kundu, reservoir consultant Bandopadhyay). Candid, transparent, technically fluent, repeatedly qualifies guidance ("oil & gas fields don't work to FY-ends"). Audio issues early. Positively received by analysts; willing to take questions offline. Tone confident but realistic about dependencies outside its control.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Q4 PAT of INR 9 cr is flattered by +INR 14 cr HPCL revenue derecognition — underlying Q4 was a loss despite high oil prices.
- Reserve "value" of $3–5 bn dwarfs current market cap framing — classic asset-rich, production-poor upstream story, entirely execution/funding-gated.
- The gas evacuation bottleneck is a multi-party national-interest negotiation, not a HOEC capex item — timing genuinely not in management's gift.
- FSO sell-down: technical (dead-stock/demurrage), not commercial — ~150k bbl is a sellable parcel; can realise at Brent without big discount.
- Accounting friction: analyst flagged inconsistent cash-flow treatment of the INR 32 cr fair-value gain vs Sept-25 disclosure; KPMG-vetted but flagged.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Funding for the B80 programme is not yet secured: "Estimated capex to be incurred in FY27: USD 45 million. Company engaging in discussions with various entities to raise funds."
- Working-capital lock-up directly deferred growth spend: "As sales revenue of ~INR 260 crore was held up due to the ongoing dispute, investments in our well drilling plans to ramp up production had to be deferred."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Reserves: 1P ~40 MMBOE (P90), 2P ~60 MMBOE (P50), 3P ~109 MMBOE (P10), independently certified. Asset value $3–5 bn (1P–2P) depending on oil price.
- 20 wells across offshore + onshore in various prep stages; "next 3 years transformational."
- Demand backdrop: acute domestic gas shortfall ("India needs every molecule"), high Brent supports realisations but also lifts rig/diesel costs.
business.title: Production / reserves outlook (demand drivers)

business.body:
- **B-80** (flagship offshore oil): 2P 26 MMBOE, only ~1 produced. Plan: 2 subsea-well workovers (post-monsoon/Nov), 3 new wells, production optimisation (lower suction pressure, compression changes), debottlenecking. MOPU + tanker capacity already in place. Target 4,000–5,000 bbl + 7.5–10 mmscf gas. Workover slipped from last quarter due to financing (INR 260 cr tied up).
- **B-15** (newly awarded offshore): in-place ~15 MMBOE, 3–5 wells in concept stage; FDP/FEED underway; 50–60 km from B-80 facility (tie-back vs separate export under study). Target 4,000–5,000 bbl + ~10 mmscf.
- **PY-1** (offshore gas, ~2 decades): platform + 55 km subsea line + onshore gas processing. Plan 2 firm wells + coiled-tubing intervention + 1 exploration + 1 contingent well (4 total). Target 12–15 mmscf. PetroVietnam (White Tiger basement reservoir) assessment positive.
- **Dirok (Assam)**: strong reservoir (Girujan/Tipam/Barail zones). Choked back to 0.3–0.4 mmscm/d vs 1.1+ capacity. 3 more wells to reach 70 mmscf; gated by DNPL/DFL pipeline.
- **Kharsang** (via GeoEnpro): drilled 9 wells, production doubled, oil + surprise gas; 9 more wells planned to double again. Gross ~700+ bbl.
- **Greater Dirok / North Dirok / Umatara**: 100% HOEC; exploration upside (North Dirok 4,000–5,000 m well, +10–15 mmscf potential).
- **Cambay (Gujarat)**: legacy; workovers, secondary recovery, low-cost incremental.
business.title: Segment / block detail

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Operates with 100% Participating Interest and no JV partners in B80 (Mumbai High, DSF), B15 (Mumbai High, Special DSF 2024), PY1 (Cauvery, Pre-NELP) and Block-19 (Assam-Arakan, OALP Round-I).
- PY1 is described as the "Only Offshore Production platform in Cauvery Offshore" and a "Unique, gas-bearing offshore fractured granitic basement reservoir in India"; its Production Sharing Contract "stands extended till October 5, 2030".
- Holds minority participating interests alongside state-owned partners: Dirok 27% (Oil India Limited 44%, Indian Oil Corporation 29%), Kharsang 35% (Oil India 40%, JEKL Pvt Ltd 25%), Palej 35% (GSPC 35%, ONGC 30%), Asjol 50% (GSPC 50%), North Balol 25% (GSPC 45%, GNRL 30%), Umatara 10% (Operator - IOCL 90%), PY3 21% (ONGC 40%, TATA Petrodyne 21%, Hardy Exploration and Production India 18%).
- On the IOCL-operated Umatara block the deck states "IOCL is the operator ; HOEC has been supporting all subsurface and drilling operations of the operator."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [HPCL Dispute] "In Aug 2025, HOEC supplied ~417,000 barrels of crude oil to HPCL. Following processing of the cargo, HPCL raised concerns regarding the presence of organic chlorides in the crude stream"; the deck elsewhere dates the dispute as "Sept 2026 | HPCL raised a dispute highlighting quality of crude oil sold; now on path of resolution". The deck states "The matter relates to a single cargo event" and that HOEC "remains committed to a transparent, technically grounded and commercially balanced resolution with HPCL while continuing to maximize value from the B-80 asset".
- [Contract Tenure] Dirok: "Revised FDP approved by MoPNG, securing the block for 10 years till 2035" with "PSC extension signing under final review with DGH/MoPNG, likely to be signed by August/September 2026"; Cambay: "PSC Extension of Block CB-ON/7 and signing of R2 area is awaited from MoPNG."
- [Litigation] PY3 (21% PI) shows Production "NA" and is "Currently in arbitration".
- [Regulatory] Block-19: "Paid extension for Initial Exploration Phase (IEP) has been obtained | Validity until Dec 2027" and the "Petroleum Exploration License (PEL) will be converted to Petroleum Lease (PL) granting flexibility in operation & production (as per New Rules 2025)".
- [Operational Risk] Umatara: first development well UTR-IOCL-1-ST hit "multiple problems relating to pressure zones, which led to sidetracking the well"; on the 2nd development well "During wireline logging , the drill string has stuck. Efforts ongoing to release the string. Sidetracking of the well is an option if the issue does not get resolved."
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Company opex ~$28/boe, stable YoY ($28.4 vs $28.6); onshore Assam lowest, B-80 offshore highest.
- Cost pressure: rig shortage (high oil price → rigs scarce/expensive), diesel shortage and high diesel cost in offshore ops; some costs uncontrollable (MOPU/tanker rentals, intra-group).
- High Brent is double-edged: better realisations but higher rig/diesel/operating costs.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** First call for new MD Mishra + ex-Shell/BG leadership. FY26 a loss year (HPCL crude-sale reversal, lower production). HPCL crude resold to third parties (Brent-minus-X), proceeds over 2–3 months. 40% Adbhoot stake acquired (+INR 32 cr non-cash exceptional). Reserves: 2P 60 / 3P 109 MMBOE. Production ~1.5 kboe/d; targets 10–11 kboe/d (Jun-2027), 22k (2028), 32k (2029). B-80 workovers slipped to post-monsoon (funding). Dirok still throttled by DNPL pipeline tie-in. Opex stable ~$28/boe. Debt/EBITDA guidance deferred.
- _next → check: (1) HPCL crude fully resold — loss or breakeven? (2) Dirok DNPL 55 km tie-in completed / gas flowing (mgmt said 1–2 months)? (3) Debt/EBITDA FY27–28 guidance + funding plan (internal vs bank vs equity)? (4) B-80 post-monsoon workovers + 3 wells progress (Nov window); (5) production trajectory toward 8,000–11,000 boe/d; (6) B-15 FDP concept selected + FEED._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- Production target: **10,000–11,000 boe/d by June 2027** (mgmt frames by drilling-season June, not 31-Mar FY-end); 22,000 by 2028; 32,000 boe/d by 2029.
- Debt / EBITDA outlook for FY27–28: **deferred to next quarter** (declined to give numbers).
- Dirok: target 70 mmscf/d (potential 45 mmscf/d), currently ~15 mmscf/d (0.3–0.4 mmscm/d gross) — gated by pipeline.
- HPCL crude: full resale to third parties expected over 2–3 months; loss/breakeven verdict by end of next quarter.
- B-15 FDP concept selection + FEED in coming months; capex/funding mix detail promised next quarter.
outlook.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Dirok potential up to ~3x (45 → 135 mmscf gross) if full pipeline (DFL–Duliajan 24" 175 km) built in 2–3 yrs.
- North/Greater Dirok exploration upside; B-15 second offshore growth leg; PY-1 basement-reservoir redevelopment.
- Associated condensate from gas fields (200–250 bbl now → 700–900 bbl at 45 mmscf) adds liquids optionality.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: New management (MD Mishra + ex-Shell/BG CFO/ops team) pitching HOEC as a sub-scale upstream turnaround: ~1.5 kboe/d today targeting 10–11 kboe/d by mid-2027 and 32 kboe/d by 2029 off a 60 MMBOE 2P / 109 MMBOE 3P base — but FY26 was a loss year (HPCL crude-sale reversal, lower production, Assam pipeline bottleneck) and the entire ramp hinges on funding, rigs and a third-party pipeline outside its control.

verdicts.item: 40 mmscfd Dirok ramp (Oil India connection) hoped by December 2024, at least by March 2025; full connectivity by August 2025 enabling up to 70

verdicts.item: Plan to build in-house oil & gas service capability (rigs, coil-tubing units) for captive drilling of ~30-well program at arm's length pricing
verdicts.note: In-house rig capability abandoned: 'owning a rig is only commercial sense if you have hundreds of wells... right now, no, we are not looking at buying rigs.'

verdicts.item: Scouting for inorganic acquisitions of producing or service assets within India (except deep waters), including Discovered Small Fields
verdicts.note: 'we acquired producing properties from an entity called Adbhoot, where we acquired the 40% share'; also increased B-80 participating interest.

verdicts.item: North-East gas grid expected operational in all forms by FY26, reversing demand constraint; DNPL line connection expected by March 2025
verdicts.note: DNPL (was March 2025) still pending; grid not operational as of June 2026.

verdicts.item: On obtaining EC, drill one 4000m exploration well plus 18 development wells for Upper Girujan in Kharsang
verdicts.note: Kharsang drilling underway; exploration/deep well pending. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Sole bidder for Block B-15 (332.4 sq km discovered small field, ~40 ft water depth) in DSF Special Bid Round 2024; will develop on government award
verdicts.note: 'B-15 is the next one that was awarded to us by the government... We are on a FDP maturation path very quickly.'

verdicts.item: Plan three PY-1 development wells with first well to commence April-June 2025 after Vietnam basement expert review
verdicts.note: PY-1 first well now FY27 (was Apr-Jun 2025).

verdicts.item: Endeavor to comfortably reach around Rs 1000 crores revenue by FY26 with margins same or slightly better as fixed costs get leveraged
verdicts.note: FY26 revenue far below Rs 1000 cr: 'Should that sale have gone through, our revenue would have been INR559 crores'; standalone net sale INR274 cr.
